field_semantics.build_rule: D4 (Riley canon, restated 2026-11-23): rematch tier tables supply SPECIES/IDENTITY ONLY. The difficulty layer builds every rematch party at battle time: 6 Pokemon, IV 31, EV <= 510 best sourced competitive set, level scaled to the player, evolving as appropriate. Identical for Pokemon and Moemon parties. A tier whose trainer_id equals tier 0's trainer_id is the source games' 'no unique rematch' row and is never a distinct battle.
field_semantics.party[].iv: ABSENT IN SOURCE — pokecrystal parties.asm records no per-mon IV for trainer parties (trainer DVs are class-level data in data/trainers/dvs.asm, not per-party values). null in this file; never a build value (build IV is 31 unconditionally, D4).
field_semantics.party[].level: IDENTITY-HISTORY ONLY — the source party's recorded level. Never a build value: battle-time level comes from the difficulty layer (opponent level = player max).
field_semantics.party[].species: IDENTITY — the only battle-facing field (D4). The species the rematch fields.

prize_money.formula: prize_base = (level of last party member) * class_base_reward
prize_money.source: pokecrystal data/trainers/attributes.asm (TrainerClassAttributes 'base reward' byte per class, constants order) + engine/battle/read_trainer_party.asm ComputeTrainerReward: wBattleReward = wEnemyTrainerBaseReward * wCurPartyLevel (level of the last party member read). Amulet Coin doubling (engine/battle/core.asm .DoubleReward) is applied on top at payout and is NOT folded into prize_base. Crystal has no double battles, so no double factor exists.

provenance: Transcribed from held pokecrystal source: data/phone/phone_contacts.asm (28 registered phone contacts), data/trainers/parties.asm (party records), constants/trainer_constants.asm (trainer consts), maps/*.asm (each contact's FightCount rematch ladder scripts), data/trainers/attributes.asm (prize base rewards). Ladder order per contact, proven from the map scripts: the script's Fight0 loads the first-battle party (the home-map placement party, which Crystal also serves as the first rematch); Fight1, Fight2, ... load the remaining same-name parties in ascending const order, each gated by a per-contact story event (full per-contact gates in phone_contact_tier_mapping.json). For 27 contacts the first-battle party is the phone const itself; HIKER Parry is the exception — his phone const is PARRY1 but his map battle and ladder head are PARRY3 (maps/Route45.asm). This table lists each distinct party once, in ladder order: tier 1 = the contact / first-battle party, tiers 2..N = the upgraded parties (113 tiers total = 28 first battles + 85 rematch parties). The Fight0 repeat of tier 1 as the first rematch is the source behaviour; it is recorded here and in tier_gates, not entered as a duplicate tier (the bound Kanto/Platinum tables likewise carry each distinct party once, with repeats expressed as same-trainer_id rows only where the source tables themselves repeat a party). FOUR CONTACTS ARE UNWIRED IN CRYSTAL: BEVERLY, IRWIN, DEREK and KENJI have no loadtrainer ladder in any script, no *_READY_FOR_REMATCH flag, and their w<Name>FightCount wram bytes are marked '; unreferenced' in ram/wram.asm — their upgraded parties exist in parties.asm but the game never loads them. They are included with derived ladder order and flagged in the mapping file: PUW's rematch layer consumes identity tables, and Crystal's unwiring is provenance, not a data gap. Identity cross-checked party-for-party against the bound Johto regional + combined trainer data. Data extraction only, under Riley's standing mechanics authorization; no downloaded code built or run.
